articles.content: Agent Manager: Run Multiple Agents Without the Chaos Kilo Blog Subscribe Sign in Agent Manager: Run Multiple Agents Without the Chaos Git worktrees, model comparison, and zero merge conflicts — without leaving VS Code Brendan O'Leary Jun 08, 2026 7 Share I’ve got six things I want an AI agent to work on right now. Refactor auth. Update docs. Add Stripe billing. Write tests. Migrate the database schema. Fix that flaky CI pipeline. The obvious move is to open six tabs and let them rip. But what actually happens is agents overwriting each other’s files, merge conflicts piling up, and context bleeding between tasks. I end up spending more time cleaning up the mess than shipping code. Agent Manager is designed to prevent that kind of overlap by isolating each task in its own worktree. What It I

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Running several agents at once used to mean accepting they’d collide, so most people just ran them one at a time. That’s a queue, not parallel work. Agent Manager gives every agent its own git worktree: separate directory on disk, separate branch, sees only its own files. Three tasks, three worktrees, all running at once.
